name: Mate with king and rook
goal: You can mate a lone king with king and rook, using your king to help and a waiting move when you need one.
intro: Mating with king and rook takes longer than with a queen, because king and rook must work together. The usual method is to build a box with the rook, protected by your own king, and make it smaller and smaller until the enemy king is pushed into a corner. No checks are needed until the final mate.

parts.title: Build the box
parts.text: First improve your king, then use the rook to fence the black king into a box.
parts.line: Kc2 Ke5 Kd3 Kd5 Ra4 Ke5 Rd4 Kf5 Re4

notes.text: Bring the king towards the centre before building the box.
The box is d8-d4-h4: the black king cannot cross the d-file or the fourth rank.

parts.title: Creep closer
parts.text: The box is e8-e4-h4. Black's king is keeping its distance, so the rook cannot shrink the box straight away.
parts.line: Kf6 Kd4 Kf5 Kd5 Kf6 Re5

notes.text: The box can't be made smaller yet, so the king creeps closer.
Back to shrinking the box: the process repeats itself.

parts.title: Shrink the box to mate
parts.text: After 8...Kf7 9.Re6 Kg7 the box is down to the last two ranks and files. Keep shrinking it with king and rook together; no checks are needed until the mate.
parts.line: Ke5 Kf7 Kf5 Kg7 Rf6 Kh7 Rg6 Kh8 Kf6 Kh7 Kf7 Kh8 Rh6#

notes.text: The king follows the rook, keeping it protected.
Black's king can only shuffle between h7 and h8. If it were your move here, you would make a waiting move with the rook along the sixth rank.
